subject: chemistry
title: Reactants to Products
welcome_lead: Watch matter rearrange itself: old substances vanish and new ones appear.
meta_desc: Understand reactants and products in chemical reactions in this KS3 chemistry adventure.
final_note: You can now read a chemical equation like a story.

concepts.def: A change where new substances are made.
The starting substances in a reaction.
The new substances made in a reaction.
Means 'reacts to produce' in an equation.
Most reactions cannot easily go backwards.

walkthroughs.body_html:
A chemical reaction takes one or more substances and turns them into new substances with new properties.

Reactants → Products

Reactants go on the left, products go on the right, and an arrow shows the direction of change.

Example: methane + oxygen → carbon dioxide + water.

When you burn magnesium, you see a bright white flame and a white powder forms.

magnesium + oxygen → magnesium oxide

The shiny metal has gone; a totally new white solid is made.

mcqs.q: What do we call the new substances made in a reaction?
In the equation 'iron + sulfur → iron sulfide', what is iron?

numericals.q: How many products are made in: hydrogen + oxygen → water?
